summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Narendra Modi Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 112/10 (48.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 145/10 (53.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: AR Patel (6/38), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, AR Patel delivered a masterclass for India (11 Wickets), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 69%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by R Ashwin (17 Runs & 7 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 10 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
